title: VAV-1 Reheat Valve Commanded But Mechanically Stuck
description: WebCTRL commands VAV-1's reheat valve normally, and the real object shows the new command was received -- but the valve actuator has physically seized, so discharge air temperature never responds.

events.description: Start Boiler-1 so reheat has a real parent heat source
AHU-1 supply fan on for airflow to exist at VAV-1
Open VAV-1 for an observable coil response
Open reheat after the parent HW loop has established temperature and pressure
Reheat valve actuator seizes at its established heating position -- WebCTRL's commands still land on the real BACnet object, but the actuator no longer moves
Relinquish the instructor command so WebCTRL/default can command closed while the simulated actuator remains physically stuck

expected_results: The HW Valve object itself keeps accepting new WriteProperty commands from WebCTRL and shows the commanded value changing
VAV-1 Discharge Temp and HW flow remain consistent with the captured 75% physical position after the displayed command is relinquished
The common HW loop load and HWS/HWR delta continue to include the stuck-open VAV coil
A student comparing 'commanded' vs 'actual discharge temp' should see the mismatch even though the point looks normal on a quick glance
completion_criteria: Student identifies that the command point and the resulting physical behavior have diverged, rather than assuming the valve command itself is wrong
Student proposes a field verification step (e.g. checking actuator position manually) rather than only re-checking software
instructor_notes: This lesson now starts Boiler-1, both required pump paths, the AHU, and VAV airflow before opening reheat; the terminal cannot create heat without its parent systems. The fault does not change the BACnet command object's value. STOP relinquishes scenario commands and restores weather targets, but thermal inventory coasts; use RESTART for a deterministic next lab.
student_objectives: Distinguish a software/network problem from a mechanical actuator failure using only available BACnet points
Understand why 'the point shows the right value' isn't proof the equipment did what was commanded
